predecessors.name: Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: Lithuania without the Memel district, which the Reich held from March 1939 (Generalbezirk Litauen, seat Kauen/Kaunas)

predecessors.name: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: Generalbezirk Weißruthenien, seat Minsk: the page says it was 'Set up across the territory of the Byelorussian SSR', including West Belarus and Nowogródek; read as Minsk and Grodno oblasts (the east…

successors.name: Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: Lithuania, retaken in July-October 1944 (Vilnius fell on 13 July 1944)

successors.name: Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: Latvia: Riga on 13 October 1944, Courland after 10 May 1945

successors.name: Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: Estonia: the mainland in September 1944, the islands by 24 November 1944

ledger.x: 25 July 1941: German civil administration of the Reichskommissariat Ostland begins.
July 1944: the Red Army enters Lithuania.
October 1944: western Lithuania is cut off and lost.
October 1944: the fighting in Lithuania ends with the Soviet breakthrough to the Baltic coast and the Courland Pocket's formation ('Formation of the Courland Pocket: 15–22 October 1944').
27 September - 24 November 1944: the Moonsund Landing takes the Estonian islands.
10 May 1945: German rule in the Baltic ends with the surrender of the Courland Pocket.
10 May 1945: the last of the Reichskommissariat Ostland ends.

wars.name: Operation Bagration
wars.outcome: The Red Army retakes Belarus and most of Lithuania between 22 June and 19 August 1944: Minsk on 3 July (the page also says 4 July), Vilnius on 13 July, Kaunas about 1 August, the Gulf of Riga coast on 31 July.

wars.name: Baltic offensive
wars.outcome: The Baltic strategic offensive (14 September - 24 November 1944) clears mainland Estonia (17-26 September), the Estonian islands (27 September - 24 November) and Riga (13 October) and seals Army Group North into the Courland Pocket (15-22 October).

certainty.note: The Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian Generalbezirke follow the borders of the Soviet republics; Weißruthenien's borders are not on the page and its eastern edge was a military-governance line (soft).
The edge is the Soviet front, which the pages date by offensives, not by line.
